# Payments and finance

Applies when the change touches: card data, ledgers, money movement. Every role loads this pack for the steps it works in, on top of its own playbook. The test commands below are best practices the gate runs: put them in the Spec's `[[tests.commands]]`, so a red one blocks the merge. Name the pack in the Spec's Context; it does not count against a Task's `skills`.

## Standards

| Standard | Edition | Checked | Source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| PCI DSS | v4.0.1; 2024 | 2026-09-28 | <https://www.pcisecuritystandards.org/document_library/> |
| SOC 2 Trust Services Criteria | 2017, with the 2022 revised points of focus | 2026-09-28 | <https://www.aicpa-cima.com/resources/download/2017-trust-services-criteria-with-revised-points-of-focus-2022> |
| ISO/IEC 27001 | ISO/IEC 27001:2022 with Amd 1:2024; ISO/IEC 27701:2025 for the privacy extension | 2026-09-28 | <https://www.iso.org/standard/27001> |
| EU Digital Operational Resilience Act | Regulation (EU) 2022/2554; applied from 2025-01-17 | 2026-09-28 | <https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2022/2554/oj> |
| Double-entry and idempotent money movement | — | 2026-09-25 (reviewed) | — |

## Checklist by loop step

| Step | Item |
| --- | --- |
| Entry (`aidd next`) | Card data, ledgers, or money movement: the financial dimension, major, the finance pool; a PCI scope change is its own decision. |
| Specify | Double-entry invariants and idempotency for every money movement in the Acceptance; reconciliation and the audit trail named. |
| Implement | No card data stored, logged, or in fixtures outside the PCI scope; amounts as integers in minor units with a currency; timestamps with an explicit zone. |
| Review | Every payment state transition is idempotent and replay-safe; failure paths reconcile. |
| Ship | The reconciliation report is clean for the observe window (the reconciliation job is the `[observe]` command); a rollback preserves the ledger with compensating entries, never deletes. |

## Test commands

| Command | Proves | How |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Ledger property tests | debits equal credits under every sequence of operations | Hypothesis, fast-check, or jqwik |
| Idempotency and replay tests | a repeated or replayed request moves money once | integration tests per money-moving endpoint |
| Secret and card-data scan | no secret or PAN in code, logs, or fixtures | gitleaks, plus a PAN pattern check on logs |
| SAST and dependency audit | no high finding at the PCI-required level | Semgrep or CodeQL; `pip-audit`, `npm audit`, or OSV-Scanner |

## Keep it current

A standard marked emerging is a draft, a first edition, or a young practice: apply it only when the change clearly needs it, and say so in the Spec. A standard checked more than a year ago is stale: `aidd eval standards` lists it, and the loop contract's research-first rule applies. When the change needs a standard this pack lacks, look up the authoritative source, record the edition in the Spec's Context, and propose the update to the aidd project's roles registry (`schemas/roles.json` in the aidd repository) as an improvement.
